messages:
maya: Poking this thread — customer reported their invoices show ~47K embedding units more than the dashboard for last week. They only sent ~9K inputs according to the UI. Invoice delta shows 56K embed units charged. :confused:

sam: Got an example account + an invoice id? any request ids from the customer? that helps trace the billing events.

maya: Account: org_8FbT, invoice INV-2026-04-07-8932. Customer pasted the CSV of inputs (9,200 rows). They say rerank + embed endpoints were both used, but dashboard per-route shows 9,200 embedding calls. Invoice line items show 56,000 embed units and 3 rerank line items.

anika: tagging billing-bot. billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-04-07-8932 shows line items: embed.units=56000, rerank.units=3000. No obvious duplicate invoice entries. Billing pipeline logs show meter events for embed consumption from trace ids: [tr_01a, tr_01b, tr_01c, tr_retry_01] — looks like multiple meter events for same client job id.

oscar: :eyes: can you share a sample request from the CSV replay? I want to check whether they used pairwise rerank (O(N^2)) or batched embeddings with pairwise pairing that would multiply charges.

maya: Customer says they used the embeddings endpoint in batches of 128 via our async batch API and then ran a separate pairwise rerank job. But their dashboard shows embed route only for ~9.2k inputs. They also see some 512-dim vectors in older runs and 256-dim in newer runs — they suspect dimensional fallback.

sam: Quick checklist: 1) Are retries happening without idempotency keys? 2) Did async batch split a single logical job into multiple worker jobs and each emitted meter events? 3) Was pairwise rerank mis-attributed to embed route in the billing join query?

oscar: I pulled the worker traces for org_8FbT. Reproducer below: when async-batcher splits a large upload we create child jobs and emit meter_event per child without deduping by parent_job_id. If a child fails and the orchestrator retries the parent, we re-emit meter events for already-completed children. So you can get duplicates.

oscar: Example failing fragment from worker logs:
```
INFO job=start id=job_7f2 split=16 parent=job_3a1 trace=tr_01a
ERROR task=encode id=job_7f2 reason=oom retrying
INFO retry schedule parent=job_3a1 new_child=job_9b4 trace=tr_retry_01
INFO meter emit trace=tr_01a units=3400 route=embed
INFO meter emit trace=tr_retry_01 units=3400 route=embed
```

maya: So duplicate meter emits both reference the same logical inputs but different trace ids. That would explain the ~x2 on some runs but not 6x.

anika: Also check vector dim billing: if the runtime falls back from quantized 512->256 dims we bill by output dim * count. Did the model variant change mid-run? billing-bot: model catalog shows model_x:v2->v2-quant fallback on 2026-04-03 at 02:12Z for region us-west. Some batches ran against v2, others against v2-quant -> different unit counts.

sam: Combine both effects (retry duplicates + dim variance + pairwise rerank attribution) and you can multiply charges non-intuitively. Need to prove by correlation of trace ids -> invoice lines -> original request ids.

maya: Action items: 1) oscar to run a replay script to reconstruct meter events for org_8FbT between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-07. 2) sam to check idempotency enforcement in async-batcher. 3) anika to mark invoice INV-2026-04-07-8932 as "under investigation" and open a provisional credit if we confirm double billing.

oscar: I'm running the replay now (script below). will attach results. Script uses our internal trace-export: `python infra/tools/replay_meter_events.py --org org_8FbT --start 2026-04-01 --end 2026-04-07 --dedupe parent_job_id`

oscar: Preliminary results: found ~28K of meter units with duplicate parent_job_id across traceranges. Deduping by parent_job_id reduces embed units from 56K -> 29K (close to dashboard 9.2K once you factor model dim differences & pairwise rerank).

anika: If dedupe reduces to ~29K, we still have a gap vs dashboard 9.2K. Next step: map route attribution. There's a billing join that uses `trace_id` to label events as embed vs rerank. If retry traces used `tr_retry_*` that may have been labeled incorrectly as embed even when rerank performed. That would still show correctly in UI if UI uses job_id to group.

sam: I'll grep the routing layer logs for `parent=job_3a1` and compare `route=` tags across traces.

maya: Customer asked for a quick workaround — recommended they run a daily cleanup to add idempotency keys on their side and re-run small batch to confirm counts. They also asked if we can provide a revised invoice immediately.

anika: I'll flag invoice for provisional credit for the delta we can directly attribute to duplicate meter events due to retries (we'll need to agree number after full replay). If we find mis-attribution between rerank/embed we'll propose an additional credit.

oscar: Follow-up: We should patch the async-batcher to emit meter events only once per parent_job_id (server-side dedupe) and add telemetry to surface `parent_job_id` on billing pipeline for easier reconciliation. Filing a PR now.

maya: Thanks team. I'll sync with customer and ask for any export of their raw job ids. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:
